sections.h2: Which Spencer County offices handle a property tax bill?
sections.html:
Three desks in Taylorsville share the work. The Property Valuation Administration (PVA) sets each parcel's value, the sheriff bills and takes payment, and the clerk's office picks up what is left after April 15. The sheriff's own website is blunt about the split: the sheriff never sets a value.

  • PVA, (502) 477-3207: assessments, exemption forms and questions about why a number changed.
  • Sheriff, (502) 477-3200: mails bills on October 1 and collects for the state, county and school districts, plus some cities and special districts such as fire protection and libraries when contracted to.
  • County attorney, (502) 477-3225: handles overdue bills from 7 West Main Street and sits with the PVA when an appeal reaches the local board.
  • County clerk, 2 West Main Street: keeps the certificates of delinquency and takes payment on any that remain unsold.

If the bill looks wrong, the PVA is the first call, and the sooner the better.

sections.h2: What should a Spencer County seller know about the area?
sections.html:
Spencer County covers 192 square miles, 187 of them land, and borders Jefferson County to the northwest. The legislature carved it from Bullitt, Shelby and Nelson counties in January 1824 and named it for Captain Spier Spencer, who died at Tippecanoe. Taylorsville has been the seat since December 1824, and Confederate guerrillas burned its courthouse in January 1865, though the county records were saved. Elk Creek is the lone census-designated place, Kentucky 44 and Kentucky 55 are the main roads, and six schools make up Spencer County Public Schools, including Hillview Academy and Taylorsville Elementary.

The county sits in the Louisville metropolitan area, and Taylorsville Lake, mostly inside the county line, is a leading local economic resource. Few places in the country grew faster early this century: from 2000 to 2005 Spencer ranked 19th among all counties by percentage growth, at 33 percent. Headcounts tell the same story: 6,801 in 1990, 11,766 in 2000, 17,061 in 2010, 19,490 in 2020 and 20,998 estimated for July 2025.

Just 255 employer establishments operated here in 2023, with 1,345 jobs on their payrolls, while residents drive farther to work than in Taylor, Todd or Trigg counties. A seller is working with a bill built on a $330,000 typical value, the highest among those four.

sections.h2: What does it cost to hold a house in Spencer County?
sections.html:
The Census figures show an expensive county by Kentucky standards. Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,795, and those without one pay $532. Households average 2.75 people, and 91.6 percent of residents stayed in the same house over the previous year.

  • 18.1 percent of residents are 65 or older, which matters for the homestead exemption described below.
  • 22.6 percent are under 18, and the 2020 census found children in 35.8 percent of households.
  • Roughly one adult in four has a four-year degree (23.6 percent), and the poverty rate is 7.5 percent.
  • The 2020 census counted 7,430 housing units, only 4.1 percent vacant, with 85.7 percent of occupied homes owner-occupied.

Shopping happens mostly elsewhere: 2022 retail sales were $79.0 million, about $3,910 per resident and the lowest rate of the four counties compared here. New construction runs the other way, with 85 building permits in 2025, the most of the four. Ask the sheriff for the exact figure on your parcel instead of estimating from the county median.

sections.h2: When is a Spencer County tax bill due, and what does paying late cost?
sections.html:
Bills carry a December 31 due date, and the sheriff's website says they go in the mail on October 1. The cost of timing is set by the collection statute:

  • Through November 1, pay 2 percent under the printed amount.
  • November 2 to December 31 is the printed amount, no more and no less.
  • January adds a 5 percent surcharge.
  • From February 1, the surcharge climbs to 10 percent and the sheriff's add-on fee joins it. The sheriff's page describes the February to April 15 stretch as a 21 percent penalty.

Escrow does not remove the need to look. The bill explains what to do when a mortgage company pays, and the sheriff's online lookup will show whether the lender actually sent the money before January begins.

sections.h2: What happens to a Spencer County bill that goes delinquent?
sections.html:
The county attorney lays the path out in order. Anything unpaid at the April 15 cutoff goes to the clerk as a certificate of delinquency, and KRS 134.122 puts a lien on the real estate. The county attorney notes the bill is also the personal obligation of the January 1 owner, with interest at 12 percent a year. Ninety days later, outside investors may buy it. The first offering is usually held in August or September.

Two things stop a sale: a payment agreement with the county attorney, or a foreclosure or bankruptcy case in which the county attorney is a party. The office also tries to reach the owner by regular mail ahead of any sale.

  • Still with the county: pay the full balance and accrued interest at the clerk's office, 2 West Main Street.
  • Already purchased: deal with the investor, who may tack on substantial administrative costs.
  • Payment plans: usually 4 to 8 months, and they must end before the next bill is due. Apply by the online form, by phone, or at 7 West Main Street, where an appointment shortens the wait. Sold certificates are not eligible.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Spencer County assessment?
sections.html:
Book a conference with the PVA first, because the process cannot begin anywhere else. After that meeting, the written appeal is filed at the clerk's office during the May window for viewing the roll, with a one-workday grace period at the end. A board of local owners then hears it about a month later.

The board wants paper: closed sales near you, an appraisal, a contractor's repair quote, an insurance declaration. If you bring none, it denies the appeal. A bill printed early uses your claimed figure, and a supplemental bill follows if the board lands higher. Ask the PVA which home sales it used for yours. That list is the fastest way to test the comparison, and parcels are physically reviewed at least every fourth year.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for the Spencer County homestead exemption?
sections.html: Owners past their 65th birthday, along with owners on a total-disability classification, can knock a fixed amount off the assessed value of the house they live in. The Department of Revenue put that amount at $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, so a $200,000 house is taxed as if it were worth $150,900. File Form 62A350 with the Spencer County PVA by December 31. An approved application carries forward while the applicant stays in the home, and a buyer must file a fresh one.

sections.h2: How are unpaid taxes handled when a Spencer County house sells?
sections.html:
Under KRS 134.015, a delinquent bill is the January 1 owner's own debt, and its lien can outlast a change of ownership for up to eleven years. Buyers and title companies look for zero balances. Ask the sheriff for this year's payoff, then ask the clerk if any certificate exists and whether an investor bought it.

When a payment agreement with the county attorney is active, say so up front so the closing agent can include the remaining balance.

faqs.q: Where do I pay a Spencer County property tax bill?
faqs.a: At the sheriff's office, (502) 477-3200. The county attorney's page says current bills can be looked up through the sheriff's website under Property Taxes, and the sheriff accepts payment until April 15.

faqs.q: What happens after April 15 in Spencer County?
faqs.a: They pass to the clerk with a lien on record, and interest at 12 percent a year starts. Investors may buy a certificate once it is 90 days old, so contact the county attorney before then.

faqs.q: Does the Spencer County attorney offer payment plans?
faqs.a: Yes, for certificates that have not been sold. Plans generally last 4 to 8 months and must finish before the next bill is due. Call (502) 477-3225.

faqs.q: How big is the Spencer County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 tax periods, taken from the home's assessed value. Apply at the PVA before year end.

faqs.q: Can a Spencer County house with back taxes be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. The lien stays on the property until the balance is paid, so the payoff is normally settled at closing. Collect figures from the sheriff and clerk beforehand.
